chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Wood-chopper's Ball and Decca's patient re-release system
summary: Decca re-released records that had not caught on, which is how Woodchopper's Ball became a hit; some early Ralph Burns arrangements were also done there.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Were there any unusually large sales records for any particular record that you had? 'The Wood-chopper's Ball' (inaudible).

Well, that was pretty good, but it was constant -- Decca had another good system, which would be wonderful if somebody picked up on it today. If they thought a thing had something but never really got off to a flying start, they wouldn't just discard it, every once in a while they would try it again. And that's what happened with 'Wood-chopper's Ball,' because it must have been out three different times. And over a period of time, several years, it became a giant.

But I don't think that's done anymore. I don't think they have the patience to wait, to see if something could happen. But whatever, I did feel that I learned a lot there, and I certainly was able to apply some of it later.
